column1: # TimeTwister eval harness configuration
# Tab-separated key/value. Read by BOTH EvalCorpusTest.kt and EvalCorpusTests.swift.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# The corpus is shared — one file, read by both cores, so a row cannot say one
# thing on Android and another on iOS. The settings the corpus is scored UNDER
# were not: the clock, the target zones, the pinned default zone, the ratchet and
# the blocking category list each existed as two independent literals in two test
# files. Nothing compared them.
# That is the same failure the shared-corpus decision was made to prevent, one
# level up. Change the clock in one core and the two would score the same rows
# under different conditions while both printed a confident "100%".
# Each harness still declares these as ordinary typed constants — they are easier
# to read that way, and a test file that fetches its own clock from a text file at
# runtime is worse, not better. What each harness now does is ASSERT its constants
# against this file. Divergence fails loudly instead of scoring silently.
# So: change a value here and in both harnesses, in the same commit.
key
# The fixed clock, as an ISO-8601 instant. Mid-May on purpose: US DST on, UK on
# BST, Australia/NZ off DST, and far from every transition, so the internal
# roll-forward-a-day heuristic cannot move an offset out from under a row.
now
# Rendered in this order, as CT / ET / PT / UK.
targets
# What a time with no zone token is attributed to.
default_zone
# The ratchet. Never lower it to make a build green — move the row to known_gap.
min_blocking_pass_rate
# Categories whose rows are regressions-not-allowed.
blocking_categories
